descriptionChirho: Thorns or thorn-bushes, used both literally and figuratively throughout the Hebrew Bible. In the primeval curse (Gen 3:18 'thorns and thistles'), in agricultural/legal contexts (Exod 22:6 thorns catching fire), as instruments of punishment (Judg 8:7, 16 thorns of the wilderness), as metaphors for worthless or wicked people (2 Sam 23:6; Ps 118:12; Isa 33:12), for desolation and judgment (Isa 32:13; Jer 4:3; 12:13; Ezek 28:24), and as a pricking brier. All number and construct forms (singular qots, plural qotsim, construct qotse) refer to the same botanical concept. Glossed as 'thorn/thorns' (eng), 'شوك' (arb), 'Dornen' (deu), '가시' (kor), 'espino' (spa), 'काँटा/काँटे' (hin).
